title: Optical analysis of AMPAR-mediated synaptic scaling in mouse hippocampus
protocol: Inject mice intraperitoneally with AM580 (20 mg/kg) or ketamine (5 mg/kg).
Anesthetize mice with a mixture of ketamine (100 mg/kg)/xylazine (10 mg/kg) via intraperitoneal injection.
Transcardially perfuse mice with ice-cold PBS for 6 minutes at 3 mL/min.
Perfuse mice with ice-cold 4% PFA in phosphate buffer for 16 minutes at 3 mL/min.
Decapitate the mouse, open the skull, and extract the brain.
Place the brain in a 15 mL conical tube containing 13 mL of 4% PFA and store for 16–24 hours at 4°C.
Transfer the brain into a 15 mL conical tube containing 13 mL of 10% sucrose in PBS and store for 16–24 hours at 4°C.
Transfer the brain into a 15 mL conical tube containing 13 mL of 20% sucrose in PBS and store for 16–24 hours at 4°C.
Transfer the brain into a 15 mL conical tube containing 13 mL of 30% sucrose in PBS and store for 16–24 hours at 4°C.
Freeze and embed the brain using OCT compound on dry ice.
Store the brain sample at −20°C.
Cut the brain into 25 μm-thick sections using a cryostat.
Transfer sections using a brush into ice cold PBS and place on ice.
Wash sections three times in 1× PBS.
Use a 12 well plate for free-floating sections.
Incubate sections with shaking gently at room temperature (RT) for one hour in blocking buffer containing 5% normal goat serum and 1% BSA without permeabilization.
Prepare primary antibody solutions specific to GluA1 or GluA2 diluted in the blocking solution.
Incubate sections overnight at 4°C with primary antibody solution on a shaker at low speed.
Gently and slowly move brain sections on the shaker to avoid tissue damage.
Wash sections with 1× PBS three times.
Incubate at RT (20°C–22°C) on the shaker at low speed (around 50 rpm) for 10 min.
Repeat washing and incubation steps two more times.
Prepare AlexaFluor 488-conjugated secondary antibody solutions at a 1:500 ratio in blocking solution.
Incubate sections with the secondary antibody solution for 2 h at RT (20°C–22°C) on the shaker at low speed.
Wash sections with 1× PBS two times.
Repeat washing and incubation steps once more.
Dilute DAPI in 1× PBS at a 1:10,000 ratio.
Incubate sections with DAPI solution for 10 min at RT (20°C–22°C) on the shaker at low speed.
Wash sections with 1× PBS once.
Repeat washing and incubation steps again.
Mount free-floating sections in 1× PBS onto a glass slide.
Place the slide with mounted section in the dark until dry.
Embed the mounted section using Aqua-Poly/Mount mounting solution and a coverslip.
Place the samples on a slide tray at RT (20°C–22°C) for overnight in the dark.
Store the sample at 4°C in the dark.
Acquire images of the dendritic region of hippocampus neurons using confocal microscopy.

Take confocal fluorescence z-stack images (0.5 μm intervals, 10 images) of the stratum radiatum in the dorsal hippocampal CA1 brain section using a ZEISS LSM 510 with a 63× objective at 1.504 × 1.504 pixels resolution.
Locate the pyramidal layer of CA1 with a 10× or 20× objective.
Focus on this region with a 63× objective and move focus to the stratum radiatum.
Take images under the same conditions of laser power and gain without saturation.
Open images in Fiji.
Project Z-stack images to single image by summation.
Save images in TIF file.
Decide threshold using Li’s minimum cross entropy algorithm.
Subtract background intensity from image.
Convert image to 8 bit.
Apply FFT band pass filter with selected criteria.
Segment adjacent puncta using the Interactive Watershed program.
Set seed dynamics to 3.
Determine intensity threshold using Li’s minimum cross entropy method.
Set peak flooding to 100%.
Allow splitting of regions.
Export regions mask.
Export binary image with H-Watershed segmentation.
Determine regions of interest (ROIs) for individual punctum using binary image particle analysis.
Set area criteria to 0.05–1 μm².
Calculate theoretical lateral resolution in confocal images as 178 nm.
Subtract background from the image before measuring areas and intensities of puncta.
Measure area and mean intensities of puncta from z-stack image with background subtraction.
Save measured values including area and intensity in an Excel worksheet.
Do not select small puncta (<0.05 μm²) for further analysis if detected due to background setting.
Calculate total intensity of puncta by multiplying the area by average intensity.
Create a list including area and total intensity for each punctum.
Exclude any secondary antibodies that could reduce imaging resolution; recommend dye use for green channel.
Generate histogram for area of puncta using GraphPad Prism.
Perform nonlinear fitting with Gaussian distribution using GraphPad Prism.
Copy the number of areas into an Excel spreadsheet.
Paste the data from Excel into GraphPad Prism.
Make a histogram with a bin width of 0.025 μm² in GraphPad Prism.
Apply Gaussian nonlinear fitting to obtain Mean and SD values.
Calculate the value of Mean + 3SD.
Select puncta that exist within the calculated area range in Excel.
Repeat this process at least three times.
Take intermediate data for analysis.
Consider intermediate data as better randomization.
